summary: England & Wales gross-negligence manslaughter very-high-culpability tier A has a 12-year starting point (range 10-18 years) under the 2018 definitive guideline.
source_citation: Sentencing Council, "Gross negligence manslaughter" definitive guideline (https://sentencingcouncil.org.uk/guidelines/gross-negligence-manslaughter/); confirmed via DWF/Pinsent Masons analyses (https://dwfgroup.com/en/news-and-insights/insights/2018/9/manslaughter-sentencing-guidelines)

summary: England & Wales gross-negligence manslaughter high-culpability tier B has an 8-year starting point (range 6-12 years) under the 2018 definitive guideline.
source_citation: Sentencing Council, "Gross negligence manslaughter" definitive guideline (https://sentencingcouncil.org.uk/guidelines/gross-negligence-manslaughter/)

summary: England & Wales gross-negligence manslaughter medium-culpability tier C has a 4-year starting point (range 3-7 years) under the 2018 definitive guideline.
source_citation: Sentencing Council, "Gross negligence manslaughter" definitive guideline (https://sentencingcouncil.org.uk/guidelines/gross-negligence-manslaughter/)

summary: England & Wales gross-negligence manslaughter lower-culpability tier D has a 2-year starting point (range 1-4 years) under the 2018 definitive guideline.
source_citation: Sentencing Council, "Gross negligence manslaughter" definitive guideline (https://sentencingcouncil.org.uk/guidelines/gross-negligence-manslaughter/)

summary: England & Wales applies a 15-year default minimum-term starting point for any other murder by an offender aged 18+ not falling within the higher paragraphs.
source_citation: Sentencing Act 2020, Sch 21, para 5 (re-enacting Criminal Justice Act 2003 Sch 21) (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2020/17/schedule/21)

summary: England & Wales sets a 25-year minimum-term starting point where the offender took a weapon to the scene intending to use it and did so, for offenders 18+ (offence on/after 2 Mar 2010).
label_raw: Murder, 25-year minimum-term starting point (weapon taken to scene)

summary: England & Wales sets a 30-year minimum-term starting point for murders of particularly high seriousness (firearm/explosive, murder for gain, sexual/sadistic, two or more victims) for offenders 18+.

England & Wales whole-life order (no fixed minimum term, effectively life with no release) applies to the most serious murders such as premeditated multiple murder or terrorist murder for offenders 21+.

England & Wales unlawful-act manslaughter culpability tier A has an 18-year starting point (range 11-24 years) under the 2018 definitive guideline, reflecting an intentional unlawful dangerous act without intent to kill.
source_citation: Sentencing Council, "Unlawful act manslaughter" definitive guideline (https://sentencingcouncil.org.uk/guidelines/unlawful-act-manslaughter/); corroborated by manslaughter offences guidelines evaluation (https://sentencingcouncil.org.uk/html-publications/evaluation-of-the-sentencing-council-s-manslaughter-offences-guidelines/)

summary: England & Wales unlawful-act manslaughter culpability tier B has a 12-year starting point (range 8-16 years) under the 2018 definitive guideline.
source_citation: Sentencing Council, "Unlawful act manslaughter" definitive guideline (https://sentencingcouncil.org.uk/guidelines/unlawful-act-manslaughter/)

summary: England & Wales unlawful-act manslaughter culpability tier C has a 6-year starting point (range 3-9 years) under the 2018 definitive guideline.
source_citation: Sentencing Council, "Unlawful act manslaughter" definitive guideline (https://sentencingcouncil.org.uk/guidelines/unlawful-act-manslaughter/)

summary: England & Wales unlawful-act manslaughter culpability tier D has a 2-year starting point (range 1-4 years) under the 2018 definitive guideline.
source_citation: Sentencing Council, "Unlawful act manslaughter" definitive guideline (https://sentencingcouncil.org.uk/guidelines/unlawful-act-manslaughter/)

summary: US federal first-degree (premeditated) murder carries USSG base offense level 43, which maps to a guideline sentence of life at Criminal History Category I.
source_citation: USSG 2A1.1; Sentencing Table level 43 = life; 18 U.S.C. 1111 (https://www.ussc.gov/guidelines/2025-guidelines-manual/annotated-2025-chapter-2-c)

summary: US federal involuntary manslaughter (criminally negligent) carries USSG base offense level 12, mapping to 10-16 months (~0.83-1.33 years) at CHC I.

source_citation: USSG 2A1.4(a)(1); Sentencing Table level 12 CHC I = 10-16 mo; 18 U.S.C. 1112 (https://www.ussc.gov/guidelines/2025-guidelines-manual/annotated-2025-chapter-2-c)
